title: JavaScript Arrays Core Check
description: Check your understanding of array creation, indexing, length, mutability, references, and basic array operations.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which syntax is the recommended way to create an array?
questions.explanation: Array literal syntax with square brackets is the standard, predictable way to create arrays.
Arrays are zero-indexed, so index `0` is the first element.
`animals.length` is `3`, so `animals.length - 1` is `2`, the last valid index.
Accessing an array index that does not exist returns `undefined`.
`const` prevents reassignment of the variable, but the array contents can still be mutated.
`push()` mutates the array and returns the new length.
`pop()` removes the last element and returns that removed value.

options.text: It throws because arrays cannot share references

questions.explanation: Assigning an array to another variable copies the reference, not the array itself.

questions.prompt: Which creates a shallow copy of an array?
questions.explanation: Spread syntax creates a new shallow array copy.
Arrays are reference types. These two arrays have the same contents but are different references.
`new Array(3)` creates an array with length 3 and empty slots, which is one reason array literals are preferred.
`at(-1)` returns the last element of the array.
